qt: to the Commission Billy Kelleher (Renew) Subject:

Bulgaria’s current Prime Minister and Energy Minister have both spoken publicly of their concerns about an agreement signed in January 2023 between the Turkish state-owned company BOTAS and its Bulgarian counterpart Bulgargaz/Bulgartransgaz. The agreement has given rise to growing concerns as to its impact on the EU’s policy to limit energy imports from Russia. In October 2023, the Commission indicated that it was reviewing the terms of the agreement. Can the Commission indicate: 1.
The full scope of its examination;
The expected time frame of the examination; and,
Whether it has the power to access all provisions of the agreement to ensure that they meet the requirements of EU law and align fully with EU energy policy.

to the Commission Clare Daly (The Left) (23 February 2024) Subject: Commission examination of the BOTAS-Bulgargaz agreement There are growing concerns that the agreement signed between the Turkish state-owned crude oil and natural gas trading company, BOTAS, and Bulgarian operator, Bulgargaz, could undermine EU energy sovereignty by giving President Erdoğan a political lever in future dealings with the EU. The agreement will allow gas, regardless of its actual origins, to be rebranded as ‘Turkish gas’ and flow via infrastructure owned or controlled by Bulgargaz into European gas networks. In addition, there are fears that arrangements in the agreement could be economically damaging to Bulgaria. In October 2023, nine months after concerns had been flagged to it about the agreement, the Commission announced that it was undertaking an examination of the agreement. Can the Commission indicate: 1.
When it expects to complete its examination of the agreement and indicate how much progress it has made to date?

Whether Bulgargaz has made available to it all documentation needed to complete its examination, including details of any conditions the agreement contains regarding the origins of gas that will come into the EU under the arrangements facilitated by the agreement?
Whether it will publish an interim report on the agreement before the final plenary session of the current EU Parliament?

Joint answer given by Ms Simson on behalf of the European Commission (10 April 2024) The Commission is closely following the developments on the Bulgarian gas market and the south-eastern region at large, in particular since the start of the unprovoked Russian war of aggression on Ukraine and the cut off of Gazprom supplies to some Member States. The Commission is in close contact with the Bulgarian authorities to support the diversification process in the region, and to ensure compatibility with EU law and avoid risks for gas supply security.

In the case at hand, the Commission has been in touch with the relevant authorities and stakeholders and has been gathering documents, views and data on the agreement, including by sending requests for information. In case of indications of non-compliance with EU law, including a breach of EU competition rules, the Commission will take appropriate action. At this point in time, however, the Commission cannot give any indication on the possible outcomes of this assessment nor on a timeline as the analysis is ongoing.
